title: Nigerian wins $100,000 NLNG prize with AI tool for faster MRI scans
source_used: The Sun Nigeria (own report by Fred Ezeh, Abuja), full text from fulltext/C10-10.txt
key_facts: Mary-Brenda Akoda, a Nigerian AI researcher, won the $100,000 Nigeria Prize for Science and Innovation, organized by Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG), for GenScan AI; the 2026 competition drew 237 entries.
She presented the technology in Abuja on Monday (5 Oct 2026) and says it can cut MRI scan time by up to 90%: a 20-minute scan to about two minutes and a one-hour exam to about six.
GenScan AI reconstructs diagnostic-quality MRI images from substantially fewer acquired data points.

According to Akoda it reached up to 99.7% similarity to conventional MRI images, and a blinded assessment by a consultant radiologist at a UK NHS hospital (Buckinghamshire) scored the images as diagnostically equivalent in all the cases assessed.
The research produced two peer-reviewed publications and two conference presentations, with support from Innovate UK, UK Research and Innovation and the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Programme.

Clinical partners are secured in the UK, US, Kenya and Nigeria, and a Nigerian diagnostic centre supports a planned pilot; next steps are regulatory submission and clinical trials, with commercial deployment targeted for the second half of 2027.
Akoda cited a health economics case study finding that even with a four-fold speed-up the technology could allow more than 40,000 additional patients to be scanned each year.
The prize's advisory board chairman said the 2025 competition had no winner because no entry met the standard.
quote_evidence: A Nigerian artificial intelligence researcher, Mary-Brenda Akoda, has won the $100,000 Nigeria Prize for Science and Innovation for developing a technology she says can reduce Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scan time by up to 90 per cent.
According to Akoda, the technology achieved up to 99.7 per cent similarity to conventional MRI images while reducing scanning time by 90 per cent.
The next steps, she said, were regulatory submission and clinical trials, with commercial deployment targeted for the second half of 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: A Nigerian-developed AI tool that could shorten MRI scans wins a national prize, but the performance figures are the inventor's own and clinical trials are still ahead.
notes: One outlet read (The Sun Nigeria); several other Nigerian outlets also carry the prize (headlines seen in the news feed). Performance figures, the radiologist check and the health economics case study are the inventor's own statements; no independent test is reported.
